- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–10 days.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ -0.5) or volatile, model often underestimates downside risk; add 3–7% buffer to forecast for next 7–14 days.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast decline, it often overshoots; cap peak forecast at 1.5x recent high or 10% below true peak.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model fails to adjust; apply mean reversion correction: subtract 1–3% per 3-day lag after sentiment reversal.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates early in horizon (first 7–10 days); apply linear decay: reduce forecast by 0.5–1% per day after day 7.
- If sentiment history shows repeated short-term reversals (e.g., 1–2 days), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with sentiment direction 1–2 days ahead.
